summary: Allegany County, Maryland, 47-foot forestry tower erected 1922 and staffed for years; removed in the 1980s; the site now holds a communications tower.

facts.status_note: Removed in the 1980s; a modern communications tower now occupies the site
facts.agency: Forest Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources)

events.note: 47-foot tower erected and ready for service in 1922, per a state forestry report for fiscal 1930; the 2007 DNR document also dates the original tower to 1922

Deed for the tower site dated 20 March 1923, recorded 19 July 1929, from the Warrior Mountain Orchard Company and Moskwa Land and Development Company; the orchard company gave permission to erect the tower
Heavy damage on Warrior Mountain and Green Ridge in May 1923; the Cumberland Evening Times reported that an investigation found the fires in the section evidently incendiary
Cumberland Evening Times (May 14, 1957) reports Mary Duvall walked to the tower for 14 years until retiring three years earlier
Approximate year: the 2007 DNR document says the tower was removed about 20 years earlier, and a photo caption says during the mid-1980s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2007 DNR document says the tower was removed about 20 years before 2007, and its photo caption says during the mid-1980s. Read together they point to roughly 1985, so the event year is approximate.

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document

notes_for_editor: The 47-foot height is the Forest Lookouts transcription of a fiscal 1930 state report, not checked against the original; the 2007 DNR report gives no height for the removed tower. The removal year is approximate (about 20 years before 2007; 'mid 1980s' caption). Staffing rests on one 1957 newspaper item and gives no start year. The DNR report (page 63) lists the tower site as a communications site and says it is reached by an unpaved road; it does not say whether the public may visit. The DNR report's own 2007 data is the newest source for the site; check it against current DNR records before publishing the 'today' paragraph. The DNR report's photo caption for the 1922 construction is in the PDF but has no direct image URL, so no photo is listed.
